Clue Benchmark is a configurable Python generator and evaluation tool for certified information availability, reliability, and evidence distribution. It creates deterministic synthetic mysteries with explicit logical rules, certifies which answers the evidence supports, and separates public agent inputs from evaluator answers. Start with your first dataset , then try distributed evidence . See research recipes , concepts , all parameters , tools and Python API , and the preliminary results gallery . No model service, account, key or repository clone is needed for the installed offline workflow. Paid model evaluation is separately authorized and never runs in the tutorials. Measured findings and original studies The latest follow-up found no consistent accuracy benefit from extra irrelevant evidence: Lite's primary endpoint stayed at 10/12, with changes on individual worlds, while Flash remained at 12/12. Costs rose roughly 56× and 77× respectively in the four-report setting. These small, exploratory results include both phases and uncertainty; they do not establish equivalence. The original-results index links the pilot, distributed-evidence controls, certified-burden study, hard cases, output-budget comparison and Qwen screening, alongside the initial follow-up and final expansion. Replay all included counts offline with clue-benchmark examples replay measured-results --output runs/results . A miniature public puzzle Ada, Ben and Cy each have one badge value: red or blue. Repeated values are allowed. The responsible person's badge is red. Ada's badge is blue. Ben's badge equals Ada's. These three truthful reports identify Cy; they do not determine every other attribute of the world. If Ben's report is missing, Ben and Cy are both possible, so abstaining is supported and a lucky Cy guess is not supported correctness. This is a teaching example, not a model measurement. See predicate semantics for the formal rules used by the generator. Version identities Software: 0.5.0rc2 . Dataset schema: clue-community-1 . Legacy flat data: 0.3.0 . docs.text: What the certificates mean Generation and validation pipeline Configuration validation → seeded sampled world → truthful core → optional evidence transformations → reliability-aware certification → partitions and coalition checks → deterministic rendering → structural duplicate/split screening → streamed bundle export → public agent views → scoring and analysis. Suspects may share motive, location, weapon or time. assignment_mode=repeated permits this; distinct forbids repeated values within an attribute and needs enough active domain values. Crime attributes match the culprit's attributes. Identifying one culprit does not identify a unique full assignment: Ada can be ruled out while her unmentioned weapon remains unknown. Reliability and interventions A truthful clue describes the sampled world. A reported statement is what an agent receives. A sampled false report changes that statement; its identity and actual false count belong to the evaluator. The public rule permits at most k false reports, including zero, one, ..., k. Trusted structural rules stay trusted; an agent cannot discard the rule that crime attributes match the culprit. Independent nuisance records introduce disjoint one-variable components. Each asserts a value in its own domain; it is satisfiable and shares no target variables. Conjoining it cannot change the target candidates. Core-entailed additions follow from the useful core; connected decoys are entailed relational additions involving target variables. Either can improve redundancy. False statements change reliability constraints. Prose padding changes presentation without adding claims. These are different interventions; extra text is not automatically harder. What is certified Total report count differs from minimum sufficient subset cost. Lower and upper bounds describe the least number of original reports needed to force the answer under the reliability rule. A lower bound is not an exact minimum until it meets an upper bound. Neither count certifies proof depth, solver difficulty, strategic diversity, or model accuracy. The production and independent Boolean encodings agree, but both use CP-SAT. Tiny exhaustive reference enumeration is engine-independent. Solver timeout or work exhaustion means unresolved , not uniqueness, inconsistency, or unsatisfiability. No supported workflow disables certification to force acceptance. A private view can be ambiguous while the global view is unique. Globally ambiguous data permits several culprits even with all reports. Inconsistent evidence permits none. A correct unsupported guess differs from a supported answer; appropriate abstention on ambiguity differs from unnecessary abstention when evidence is sufficient. Coalition checks currently cover at most eight agents and can be expensive. Reports retain their original identities when replicated/forwarded. Deterministic bounded report forwarding is a programmed protocol, not learned conversation, free-form dialogue, or a communication-emergence claim. Seeds, splits and duplicates Deterministic generation screens structural fingerprints and renamings. World-hash allocation keeps paired variants in the same split; configured holdout families go to transfer. Screening detects selected structural symmetries, not every equivalent strategy or reasoning shortcut. Family holdout does not prove out-of-distribution competence. English comes from templates, never an LLM. Internal IDs are S01, S02, ...; presentation permutes Person/Entity numbers with naming_seed . Default domains are weapon (Rope, Wrench, Poison, Knife), location (Study, Kitchen, Library, Garden), motive (Revenge, Inheritance, Jealousy, Blackmail), and time (20:00, 21:00, 22:00, 23:00). Customize puzzle.config.domains with distinct nonempty strings and inspect the resolved configuration. Quotes and unicode are JSON escaped by the formatter.

docs.text: Four worked research recipes Each recipe keeps logical guarantees separate from observed model behavior. Use a new output directory; none of these commands invokes a model. Independent nuisance dose Question: can more irrelevant evidence improve a weaker model's supported accuracy? noise-volume generates one four-necessary-report branching world with 100 satisfiable independent records, no false reports, single-agent complete evidence, and the useful stream in front. clue-benchmark generate-dataset --preset noise-volume --output runs/noise clue-benchmark examples replay measured-results --output runs/counts The motivating low-thinking Lite counts were 2/5, 3/5, 5/5 at 0/100/1000 records on the same five worlds. Flash was 5/5 throughout. In the eight-report stratum Lite was 5/8, 5/8, 4/8, including one provider failure at the largest dose. This is not established noise-assisted reasoning: one attempt per condition, some identical payloads elsewhere changed answers, and input costs rose sharply. The fixed endpoint was Lite's 1000-minus-zero change in the four-report stratum, with two attempts averaged per world. The initial study plus one final expansion completed twelve worlds and 144 scored calls plus two initial probes. Combined Lite counts were 10/12, 9/12, 10/12 in the primary stratum and 9/12, 5/12, 7/12 in the eight-report stratum; Flash scored 12/12 throughout. Six worlds per stratum give limited precision. The primary estimate is zero with a descriptive 95% world-bootstrap interval [-25, +25] points; unchanged scores are not proof of equivalence. The combined estimate is explicitly exploratory because expansion followed the initial result. Estimated total $6.96 , no holds, below $10. See separate phases and replay . To prepare a new exact study offline, supply explicit reviewed model prices and every prior measured bank: clue-benchmark prepare-nuisance-followup --models models.json --prior-bank prior/bank --output runs/followup This command prepares candidates and maximum reservations only. It cannot authorize inference. Recognizable records differ from adversarial prose; the design changes context length and composition together and cannot identify a mechanism. Complete/private/shared evidence Question: does the receiver have enough information? Use distributed and the eight-world replay tutorial . The complete views are unique; private views are ambiguous, and bounded forwarding retains report identities. The observed star success is a property of this protocol and fixture, not a universal topology ranking. False-report robustness clue-benchmark generate-dataset --preset false-reports --output runs/false clue-benchmark explain-config --preset false-reports Question: can an agent reason under an at-most-k rule? The preset publishes allowance two with one sampled false report; actual corrupted identities are private. Final uniqueness is certified under the published rule. The historical fixed-allowance experiment scored Lite 8/8, 7/8, 8/8 and Flash 8/8 throughout at 0/1/2 actual corruptions. Necessary evidence was not held fixed. This small result is not monotonic evidence of difficulty. Burden and resource limits clue-benchmark generate-dataset --preset hard-example --output runs/hard This small bounded example has eight suspects and eight necessary reports. It is not the measured large hard regime. At 32 necessary reports, historical Flash scored 30/30 in two path/tree arms while Lite scored 9/30 and 7/30, from three attempts on ten worlds per arm. Simple construction heuristics solve some families. The fresh large confirmation scored 9/48 correct, 28 wrong and 11 abstentions with 64 suspects, 455 interacting reports and 32768 output tokens including thinking; no protocol/provider failures. The reports were not individually necessary. A prior adaptive six-world example improved from 2/6 to 5/6 with larger output allowance. Resource budgets materially affect interpretation. Do not merge these settings into one model score.

docs.text: Bundle data dictionary and dataset card Every community bundle contains five files. cases.jsonl streams one public case header followed by report rows ( kind , case_id , report_id , deterministic text , formal constraint ). Headers include suspect IDs/domains, display names, assignment rule, public corruption allowance, report count and presentation identity. partitions.jsonl maps each original report ID to its owner agent IDs and partition identity. answers.jsonl is evaluator-only: sampled solution, possible culprits, actual false report IDs, core report IDs and nuisance count. certificates.jsonl is evaluator-only: answerability, sufficient-subset bounds, witnesses, reliability/coalition checks and partition quotas. manifest.json identifies schema/software/solver, resolved config/config hash, SHA-256 for the other four files, source/checkpoint identity, world/split list, metrics and explicit release gates. The manifest is not an agent input: it can expose evaluator metrics and seeds. Checksums detect changes, not human approval, originality, logical depth, or license clearance. Public export uses positive case/report/constraint field allowlists and does not copy the manifest, partitions, evaluator files, checkpoints, ledgers or receipts. Anyone releasing labels for reproduction must keep them out of agent input directories. Scope and provenance Synthetic worlds, deterministic templates and configured domains; no human cases or personal records are required. Coverage depends on selected families, types, domains and acceptance filters. Rejection sampling changes observed frequencies. Known shortcuts exist in construction families; certified information cost is not a certified hardness scale. Splits use world hashes with optional family transfer overrides; paired variants share a world split. Appropriate uses include evidence sufficiency controls, reliability reasoning, abstention, communication delivery and bounded reproducible demonstrations. Do not infer real-world investigative skill, universal frontier-model weakness, human validation, or learned collaboration from these scores. Code license proposal: Apache-2.0. Dataset/prose proposal: CC BY 4.0. Neither is granted by this candidate; ownership clearance is pending. No hosted dataset URLs, Croissant distribution URLs, DOI or public upload is claimed. Large measured archives remain separate private artifacts until screened and cleared. The wheel contains only tiny example data and sanitized assignment outcomes for offline reanalysis. Packaged nuisance measurement dictionary The measured-results resource nuisance-followup.json uses clue-nuisance-measurements-1 . episodes contains all 144 scored slots; phase is initial or extension, and burden , dose , world_id , model , repeat identify the matched design. answer , supported/correct/abstained/protocol flags and sufficiency labels are evaluator outcomes. input_tokens , output_tokens (including thinking), thinking_tokens , latency seconds and integer microdollar estimates preserve resource costs. Request IDs remain unique per dispatched attempt. The accounting header includes the two initial probes and the combined $10.00 cap; scored panel costs exclude probes and are not provider invoices. Current software is 0.5.0rc2; measured generation/evaluation sources were 0.5.0rc1 and remain frozen separately. The post-result expansion is labeled; combined summaries are exploratory. Resource and source indexes verify hashes. No credentials, human authorization evidence, SQLite ledgers, raw receipt bodies or provider prose are part of these distribution copies. Public agent exports never read this evaluator measurement resource.

docs.text: Every community bundle contains five files. cases.jsonl streams one public case header followed by report rows ( kind , case_id , report_id , deterministic text , formal constraint ). Headers include suspect IDs/domains, display names, assignment rule, public corruption allowance, report count and presentation identity. partitions.jsonl maps each original report ID to its owner agent IDs and partition identity. answers.jsonl is evaluator-only: sampled solution, possible culprits, actual false report IDs, core report IDs and nuisance count. certificates.jsonl is evaluator-only: answerability, sufficient-subset bounds, witnesses, reliability/coalition checks and partition quotas. manifest.json identifies schema/software/solver, resolved config/config hash, SHA-256 for the other four files, source/checkpoint identity, world/split list, metrics and explicit release gates. The manifest is not an agent input: it can expose evaluator metrics and seeds. Checksums detect changes, not human approval, originality, logical depth, or license clearance. Public export uses positive case/report/constraint field allowlists and does not copy the manifest, partitions, evaluator files, checkpoints, ledgers or receipts. Anyone releasing labels for reproduction must keep them out of agent input directories.

docs.text: Synthetic worlds, deterministic templates and configured domains; no human cases or personal records are required. Coverage depends on selected families, types, domains and acceptance filters. Rejection sampling changes observed frequencies. Known shortcuts exist in construction families; certified information cost is not a certified hardness scale. Splits use world hashes with optional family transfer overrides; paired variants share a world split. Appropriate uses include evidence sufficiency controls, reliability reasoning, abstention, communication delivery and bounded reproducible demonstrations. Do not infer real-world investigative skill, universal frontier-model weakness, human validation, or learned collaboration from these scores. Code license proposal: Apache-2.0. Dataset/prose proposal: CC BY 4.0. Neither is granted by this candidate; ownership clearance is pending. No hosted dataset URLs, Croissant distribution URLs, DOI or public upload is claimed. Large measured archives remain separate private artifacts until screened and cleared. The wheel contains only tiny example data and sanitized assignment outcomes for offline reanalysis.

docs.text: The measured-results resource nuisance-followup.json uses clue-nuisance-measurements-1 . episodes contains all 144 scored slots; phase is initial or extension, and burden , dose , world_id , model , repeat identify the matched design. answer , supported/correct/abstained/protocol flags and sufficiency labels are evaluator outcomes. input_tokens , output_tokens (including thinking), thinking_tokens , latency seconds and integer microdollar estimates preserve resource costs. Request IDs remain unique per dispatched attempt. The accounting header includes the two initial probes and the combined $10.00 cap; scored panel costs exclude probes and are not provider invoices. Current software is 0.5.0rc2; measured generation/evaluation sources were 0.5.0rc1 and remain frozen separately. The post-result expansion is labeled; combined summaries are exploratory. Resource and source indexes verify hashes. No credentials, human authorization evidence, SQLite ledgers, raw receipt bodies or provider prose are part of these distribution copies. Public agent exports never read this evaluator measurement resource.

docs.text: CLI, Python and native tools Current commands clue-benchmark --help is the installed command inventory. --version prints the software identity. All offline commands work without provider/figure/docs extras. presets list lists purpose; presets show NAME includes resolved values. generate-dataset and profile-dataset accept exactly one of --preset NAME or --config PATH . Explicit --output and --workers override either source. explain-config accepts the same config selectors and overrides; it returns resolved values with authored field descriptions. validate-dataset DIRECTORY checks the five-file bundle and independent semantics. export-public DIRECTORY --agent 0 --output FILE writes allowlisted public case/report JSONL only. inspect-case DIRECTORY [--case-id ID] [--agent 0] returns public evidence for one case. examples replay distributed-evidence --output DIRECTORY recomputes solver information controls. examples replay nuisance-followup --output DIRECTORY recomputes the initial, final expansion and exploratory combined study; optional --figures writes plots. examples replay measured-results --output DIRECTORY recomputes all packaged historical panels, preserving study/model/arm/condition denominators. report SOURCE.json --output DIRECTORY writes local HTML, exact source JSON and a machine-readable report. It never runs inference. prepare-nuisance-followup prepares offline matched inputs and full-study costs; it grants no execution permit. Invalid inputs and incomplete work use status 2 with actionable stderr errors. Normal command summaries are JSON on stdout. Exports/reports/replays refuse overwrites. Generation resumes only matching source/config checkpoints. A frozen evaluation plan rejects drift. Python public API from clue_benchmark import ( resolve_config, generate_dataset, validate_dataset, iter_cases, export_public, inspect_case, evaluate_agent, ) config = resolve_config(name="quickstart", output="runs/python-demo") generate_dataset(config) validate_dataset("runs/python-demo") export_public("runs/python-demo", "runs/python-agent.jsonl", agent_id=0) print(inspect_case("runs/python-demo", agent_id=0)["rules"]) result = evaluate_agent("runs/python-demo", lambda view: {"kind": "abstain"}) CommunityConfig , generate_case , partition , score and profile_dataset remain available. iter_cases streams public bundle rows. evaluate_agent supplies copies of public fields to a trusted callable; it owns the evaluator labels. This is an API boundary, not process isolation. Run untrusted code separately with only exported public files, then score its returned actions in the evaluator process. Native actions and evaluation The supported final actions are answer(target) and abstain() . target must be a listed internal suspect ID, not the display name. Python response dictionaries are {"kind":"answer","target":"S01"} or exactly {"kind":"abstain"} . Missing, malformed or extra actions are protocol failures, separately reported from wrong supported-context answers. prepare-community-evaluation DIRECTORY --models models.json --output plan.json --ceiling-microdollars INTEGER freezes explicit models, prices and settings. Conditions: complete, independent private views, sharing. Graphs: star, ring, chain, complete. Defaults: all three conditions, complete graph, three rounds, 64 reports/message, one repeat, structured_text input. CLI --input-view text_only omits formal constraints; do not pool with structured_text results. Each model supplies id, vendor, model, settings, context_tokens, input/output_microdollars_per_million_tokens; optional identity is an exact expected returned string, tokenizer_identity is descriptive. Vendor-specific settings are validated. Output allowances include thinking when the provider bills it. One dollar is 1,000,000 microdollars. Conservative serialized-byte bounds include tool overhead. Overflow is rejected, never truncated. run-community-evaluation plan.json --dataset DIRECTORY --output RUN --dry-run serializes/preflights without credentials or network. --execute --authorization human.json requires the human plan-bound contract; the command never creates approval. Request timeouts are 600 seconds, retries zero. Persistent SQLite reservations survive interruption and concurrent launches. Settled usage plus unresolved maxima must fit the plan cap. Unknown usage or identity/resource breaches stop and hold funds. Never release holds by guessing or edit the ledger. The new $10.00 study additionally requires one shared allocation across every child plan and probe; a cap per arm is forbidden. Legacy appendix Flat generate , validate , export , the legacy Config API and v0.3 archives retain their original shapes. They are not aliases for community bundles. Old investigation/request-clue interfaces are historical; current modes are complete, independent private views and bounded report forwarding. run-nuisance-followup DIRECTORY preflights every frozen scored/probe plan offline. Its explicit --execute --authorization human.json mode serializes the entire study, checks the sum of child ceilings, and stops all later jobs on unknown usage or a failed native compatibility probe. Fixed child ledgers prevent replay on resume. Human approval binds manifest_id , the $10.00 cap and exact total request count; the current candidate permits 96 scored slots plus at most two compatibility calls. No authorization is generated by preparation. analyze-nuisance-followup DIRECTORY --output NEW_DIRECTORY writes per-call JSONL and a machine-readable analysis. It preserves never-dispatched slots and leaves completed-panel accuracy and paired effects null while execution is incomplete. Completed studies use world-level two-attempt means, descriptive cluster bootstrap, exact sign-flip analysis and between-model differences. No paid model is called. unpack-archive FILE.tar.gz --sha256 PUBLISHED_HASH --output NEW_DIRECTORY handles explicit local reproduction downloads. It verifies the checksum before extraction, rejects links/traversal/duplicate paths, and enforces a declared uncompressed byte limit ( --maximum-bytes , default one billion). No hosted URLs or download service are claimed until the owner clears and publishes the artifacts. Output safety in 0.5.0rc2 Completed matching datasets are returned without solver work or file rewrites. Generation and native evaluation take an exclusive per-directory lock on Linux and macOS; simultaneous writers receive a short error. A request whose atomic reservation was lost to another launcher is never dispatched. Ledger identity creation is serialized. Unknown usage still stops and holds the maximum. JSON files use unique temporary files and atomic publication. Public exports and new evaluator outputs use atomic no-clobber publication. An occupied evaluator output is rejected before invoking an agent callback. Reports validate source shape before creating output, escape arbitrary text and retain exact source JSON; phase-separated result tables are keyboard-scrollable.

docs.text: Complete generation parameter reference Defaults below come directly from the current dataclasses; descriptions are authored and coverage is tested. All fields affect local generation/certification only; none authorizes paid inference. Examples show JSON leaf values: place them at the named path. Bounds/compatibility and invalid combinations are stated with each description. Evaluation/tool controls and troubleshooting are separate. puzzle.family Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "standard" . Construction family: standard, pairwise, cross_attribute, equality_tree, branching, redundant_paths. Family-specific enabled types must remain available. A family is not a difficulty guarantee. puzzle.assignment_mode Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "repeated" . repeated permits shared attribute values; distinct requires at least suspect_count active values in every domain and forbids equality families. puzzle.extra_clue_scope Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "all" . all samples from all attributes; non_target_attributes requires branching/equality_tree and at least two attributes. puzzle.attribute_mismatches Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional integer 1..number of attributes; only redundant_paths. Controls how many attribute anchors differ from the culprit. puzzle.config.suspect_count Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 4 . Integer 2..64 suspects. More suspects increase encoding size and subset search; no universal accuracy prediction. puzzle.config.domains Type: <class 'dict'> . Resolved default / JSON example: {"location": ["Study", "Kitchen", "Library", "Garden"], "motive": ["Revenge", "Inheritance", "Jealousy", "Blackmail"], "time": ["20:00", "21:00", "22:00", "23:00"], "weapon": ["Rope", "Wrench", "Poison", "Knife"]} . Map of 1..8 nonempty attribute names to 2..32 distinct strings. Domains may contain unicode/quotes. Changing values changes the world identity. Default lists are printed in the resolved configuration. puzzle.config.clue_count Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 8 . Positive integer core reports, before evidence transformations. Must cover all configured minima. Equality constructions require at least suspect_count; redundant_paths requires (suspect_count+1)*attributes. puzzle.config.enabled_types Type: <class 'tuple'> . Resolved default / JSON example: ["crime_different_from", "crime_negative", "crime_positive", "crime_same_as", "indirect_negative", "indirect_positive", "suspect_different_from", "suspect_same_as", "unary_negative", "unary_positive"] . Nonempty unique list of the ten supported clue predicates. Constructed families require their named predicates; see predicate reference. puzzle.config.alpha Type: <class 'float'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0.7 . Sampling weight/control in [0,1]. Direct category weight alpha; indirect category weight 1-alpha. Construction also uses alpha when choosing available direct versus relational anchors. Rejection and availability condition these weights. puzzle.config.beta Type: <class 'float'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0.75 . Conditional positive relationship weight in [0,1] within indirect sampling, with complement for negative relationships. Availability and rejection alter realized frequencies; not a measured difficulty slider. puzzle.config.min_murderer_links Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 1 . Nonnegative integer lower bound on murderer-link reports, at most clue_count. Hard accepted-case filter. puzzle.config.max_murderer_links Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional nonnegative integer upper bound, no smaller than the minimum. Impossible limits exhaust candidates. puzzle.config.max_positive_murderer_links Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional nonnegative cap on positive murderer links; may conflict with available family anchors. puzzle.config.min_indirect_clues Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0 . Nonnegative minimum number of indirect reports, at most clue_count. Requires enabled indirect types. puzzle.config.min_unique_subset_size Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 1 . Positive minimum sufficient subset size, at most clue_count. Community sufficient bounds cannot undercut this legacy minimum. puzzle.config.require_indirect_essential Type: <class 'bool'> . Resolved default / JSON example: false . Boolean hard requirement: at least one indirect clue is essential; impossible with no indirect types. puzzle.config.min_pairwise_clues Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0 . Nonnegative required suspect-comparison count, at most clue_count. May reject unsupported families. puzzle.config.active_values_per_attribute Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional integer 2..smallest domain size. Distinct assignment also requires at least suspect_count active values. puzzle.config.reasoning_route Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "standard" . standard, pairwise or cross_attribute legacy construction route. Keep standard for equality constructions; family and route must agree. puzzle.config.max_attempts Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 64 . Positive bounded legacy construction attempts per candidate; increasing it costs solver time and does not relax semantic filters. puzzle.config.mutation_steps Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 12 . Nonnegative legacy search mutation steps. Zero skips mutation; it does not skip certification. puzzle.config.max_solver_calls Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 10000 . Positive maximum legacy solver calls. Exhaustion means unresolved, never a proof. puzzle.config.solver_seconds Type: <class 'float'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 2.0 . Positive per-solve wall-time seconds in legacy construction. Timeouts mean unresolved. puzzle.config.solver_work Type: <class 'float'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0.2 . Positive CP-SAT deterministic work bound. Engine-specific effort units; unrelated to model reasoning depth. puzzle.config.generation_seconds Type: <class 'float'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 30.0 . Positive total legacy generation wall-time seconds. Independent of community certification_seconds. evidence.minimum_sufficient_clues Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional nonnegative certified lower bound in reports. Must not exceed maximum or undercut legacy minimum; ambiguous cases forbid it. evidence.maximum_sufficient_clues Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional nonnegative certified upper bound in reports; ambiguous cases forbid a sufficient subset. evidence.entailed_clues Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0 . Nonnegative count of extra core-entailed reports. Can improve redundancy and model performance; increases text and certification cost. evidence.connected_decoys Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0 . Nonnegative count of extra relational entailed reports connected to target variables. Different from independent nuisance. evidence.irrelevant_records Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0 . Nonnegative count of satisfiable independent one-variable components, appended by default. Above 1000 requires large_corpus=true. Increases export and model input cost. evidence.false_reports Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0 . Integer 0..2 actual sampled corruptions; private evaluator information. Cannot exceed corruption_allowance. evidence.corruption_allowance Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: 0 . Optional integer 0..2 public at-most-k rule; resolves to false_reports when omitted. At most is not exactly k. evidence.answerability Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "unique" . unique or ambiguous after all reports and the reliability rule. Ambiguous requires null sufficient bounds and null minimum coalition size. evidence.corruption_strategy Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "random" . random or targeted. Targeted false reports require unique answerability and may increase solver search. evidence.corruption_search_attempts Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 12 . Positive targeted-search attempt cap. Exhaustion retains rejection evidence; never implies success. evidence.maximum_alternative_margin Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional positive maximum alternative reliability margin; requires unique answerability. Extra solver profiling cost. distribution.agent_count Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 2 . Integer 1..8. Explicitly use one for single-agent work; default two. Coalition enumeration grows exponentially. distribution.shared_reports Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0 . Nonnegative count visible to every agent, no larger than total report count. distribution.private_replication Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 1 . Integer 1..max(1,agent_count-1) owners per non-shared report; repeated presentation retains original report identity. distribution.per_agent_quotas Type: list[int] | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional exact nonnegative report counts, one per agent. Must be feasible with sharing and replication; impossible quotas reject candidates. distribution.minimum_coalition_size Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: 2 . Optional integer 1..agent_count. Hard certified minimum team size; null for globally ambiguous data. distribution.max_attempts Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 128 . Positive bounded partition-search retries; more retries cost certification time, not a relaxed quota. presentation.theme Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "mystery" . mystery or investigation. Uses Person/Entity labels, deterministic wording and no LLM. presentation.naming_seed Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0 . Integer seed for label permutation, independent of the sampled world; labels are not real people. presentation.template Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "compact" . compact or expanded deterministic report wording. Expanded adds a fixed sentence to each report. presentation.clue_order Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "shuffle" . shuffle, canonical or reverse. Shuffle uses a deterministic seed; canonical sorts report hashes. presentation.evidence_placement Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "front" . front, middle, end or interleaved position of core reports within the independent nuisance stream. presentation.minimum_words Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional nonnegative minimum whitespace word count. Adds explicitly nonfactual template padding when necessary. presentation.maximum_words Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional nonnegative maximum whitespace word count. Evidence is never truncated; impossible bounds reject. presentation.minimum_tokens Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional nonnegative lower token bound. Requires Python tokenizer with stable identity and workers=1; not provider chat billing. presentation.maximum_tokens Type: int | None . Resolved default / JSON example: null . Optional nonnegative upper token bound; same tokenizer constraints. Overflow rejects instead of shortening reports. dataset.count Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 1 . Positive accepted-world target. Candidate exhaustion writes incomplete status and CLI exits 2. dataset.seed Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 0 . Nonnegative first candidate seed; candidates increase in deterministic order. Resume reuses recorded candidate receipts. dataset.workers Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 1 . Positive process count. Does not change config fingerprint or accepted seed order. Custom tokenizer requires one worker. dataset.splits Type: <class 'dict'> . Resolved default / JSON example: {"development": 0.8, "test": 0.2} . development/test/transfer proportions, finite nonnegative values summing to one. Hash-based allocation keeps paired worlds together. dataset.holdout_families Type: list[str] . Resolved default / JSON example: [] . List of valid families forced to transfer split; family holdout is not a proof of strategy diversity. dataset.output_directory Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "community-output" . Nonempty local directory. Existing matching checkpoints resume; source/config drift rejects. Keep frozen measured runs separate. dataset.certification_seconds Type: <class 'float'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 60 . Positive community certification wall-time seconds per candidate. Includes coalition checks; unresolved timeouts reject. dataset.max_solver_calls Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 20000 . Positive community certification call budget. Separate from nested legacy generation controls. dataset.max_candidates_per_case Type: <class 'int'> . Resolved default / JSON example: 20 . Positive candidate multiplier; total attempted candidates bounded by count times this value. dataset.large_corpus Type: <class 'bool'> . Resolved default / JSON example: false . Boolean explicit opt-in for more than 1000 independent records. Does not authorize inference or raise any monetary cap. schema_version Type: <class 'str'> . Resolved default / JSON example: "clue-community-1" . Exact wire contract clue-community-1. Separate from software and presentation identity; stale schemas are rejected.

docs.text: Every active clue predicate Let x(s,a) be suspect s's value for attribute a, and c the responsible suspect. Crime values equal x(c,a). A report can be false only under the public at-most-k rule; structural rules stay trusted. Values may repeat unless distinct is explicit. In the examples below, A and B are suspect IDs, color has red/blue, and room has hall/study. Unmentioned assignments are arbitrary permitted values. unary_positive English: Suspect "A" has "color" = "red". Formal: x(A,color)=red. Satisfying: A red. Counterexample: A blue. unary_negative English: Suspect "A" has "color" != "red". Formal: x(A,color)≠red. Satisfying: A blue. Counterexample: A red. crime_positive English: The murderer has "color" = "red". Formal: x(c,color)=red. Satisfying: culprit A red. Counterexample: culprit A blue. crime_negative English: The murderer has "color" != "red". Formal: x(c,color)≠red. Satisfying: culprit A blue. Counterexample: culprit A red. This is categorized as indirect by the current sampling code; everyday language categories can differ. crime_same_as English: The murderer has the same "color" value as suspect "A". Formal: x(c,color)=x(A,color). Satisfying: culprit B blue, A blue. Counterexample: culprit B red, A blue. This does not assert c=A; sharing values is allowed. crime_different_from English: The murderer has a different "color" value as suspect "A". Formal: x(c,color)≠x(A,color). Satisfying: culprit B red, A blue. Counterexample: culprit B blue, A blue. With c=A this report is always false. suspect_same_as English: Suspects "A" and "B" have the same "color" values. Formal: x(A,color)=x(B,color). Satisfying: both red. Counterexample: A red, B blue. suspect_different_from English: Suspects "A" and "B" have different "color" values. Formal: x(A,color)≠x(B,color). Satisfying: A red, B blue. Counterexample: both red. indirect_positive English: At least one suspect has "color" = "red" and "room" = "hall". Formal: ∃s: x(s,color)=red ∧ x(s,room)=hall. Satisfying: A red/hall. Counterexample: A red/study and B blue/hall. The same suspect must satisfy both halves; this does not identify the culprit. indirect_negative English: No suspect has both "color" = "red" and "room" = "hall". Formal: ¬∃s: x(s,color)=red ∧ x(s,room)=hall. Satisfying: A red/study and B blue/hall. Counterexample: A red/hall. This does not forbid red alone or hall alone. record_positive English: Record COMPONENT: its independent value equals "0". Formal: y(COMPONENT,value)=0 with declared domain {0,1}, disjoint from target variables. Satisfying: that component's value 0. Counterexample: that value 1. Each generated component has one such in-domain assertion, so it is satisfiable; conjoining the stream leaves target candidates unchanged. This is not an entailed fact about suspects and does not assert anything about culprit attributes.

docs.text: Troubleshooting Distinct values exhausted: expand every domain/active-value set or reduce suspects; equality families require repeated assignments. Family/types disagree: restore required predicates or choose a compatible family/route. Redundant paths needs exactly n+1 reports per attribute. Impossible quotas/coalition: check shared count, replication, per-agent sums and agent limits (at most eight). A retry limit does not make impossible quotas feasible. Ambiguous with a sufficient subset: set sufficient bounds and minimum coalition to null; do not claim a unique answer. Tokenizer absent: supply a stable-identity tokenizer via Python with workers=1, or remove token constraints. Do not silently switch tokenizers. Impossible word/token bounds: raise the bound or explicitly change the requested evidence. Evidence is never truncated to fit. Candidate exhaustion: inspect saved rejection reasons and choose a new output config/directory. Incomplete is exit 2, not a complete bank. Solver timeout/work exhaustion: unresolved; use a declared larger offline budget on fresh outputs. Never disable certification. Context overflow: reject before dispatch. Do not omit evidence or shrink an answer budget after freezing a matched study. Malformed tools/missing final action: retain a protocol failure and inspect the saved finish reason separately from wrong answers. Provider error/model drift/unknown usage: stop. Preserve returned identity, safe receipt and maximum reservation. Use the documented reconciliation procedure; never edit ledger balances or assume zero cost. Held funds/interruption: resume with the same plan, sources and durable ledger. An unresolved dispatch must not replay automatically; zero retries is intentional. Stale schema/source/config: use the frozen historical source for historical plans, or prepare a new plan/output explicitly. Do not rewrite hashes to make a plan pass. docs.text: Preliminary measured results These are separate historical studies with different thinking budgets, input shapes, adaptive/fresh status and denominators. No pooled leaderboard is supported. Recompute from sanitized per-assignment records without credentials: The initial-preview open questions separate unanswered research questions from pending full-release decisions. clue-benchmark examples replay measured-results --output runs/measured With the optional figures extra installed, add --figures to reproduce the paired accuracy/cost SVG. The command writes results.json and an accessible local HTML report with study-specific tables, source hashes and assigned counts. What is interesting about the follow-up? The pilot's apparent benefit from irrelevant evidence did not repeat consistently . Lite's four-report endpoint accuracy was unchanged on average, but that average hid one improving world and one worsening world, with four unchanged. The eight-report dip at 100 extra records and partial recovery at 1,000 is a possible distraction signal, not an established dose-response pattern. Flash stayed at the ceiling in this narrow setting. The most consistent tradeoff was cost: roughly 56× for Lite and 77× for Flash at 1,000 extra records, without higher aggregate endpoint accuracy. These results make a useful replication and robustness example. They do not prove that irrelevant evidence never helps or hurts. The small sample and post-result expansion require exploratory interpretation; the full phase results below retain uncertainty and all conditions. Where to find the original results The earlier studies have not been replaced by the new follow-up. Their sanitized outcomes are included in both the installed offline gallery and this documentation: Original nuisance pilot and information availability : pilot assignments . Certified evidence burden : hardness assignments . Fresh hard cases : 48-world assignments ; the adaptive output-budget assignments are a separate study. Qwen completion and correctness : screening outcomes . Initial October 27 follow-up : original 96-call analysis and original reproduction index . Final expansion and exploratory combined result : separate phase summaries , 144 assignments with phase identities and combined reproduction index . The historical source/checksum index records original source locations and hashes. The original documents, frozen study sources and operational archives remain preserved in the private checkout; distribution copies omit credentials and operational records. Full raw archives are not publicly deployed. Saved evaluator outcomes must never enter agent prompts. The same five worlds appear at all doses, with one attempt each. Additional context cost more. This small positive Lite observation is a hypothesis, not a general claim that weaker agents benefit from noise. Information availability Eight worlds: Flash 8/8 complete answers, 32/32 appropriate abstentions on ambiguous private views, and 8/8 answers when one-round star forwarding delivered the needed evidence. Lite made two lucky correct ring guesses with insufficient evidence. Forwarding was programmed. The offline tutorial reproduces solver controls separately from these model counts. Nuisance records Original pilot Four necessary reports: Lite 2/5, 3/5, 5/5 at 0/100/1000 records; Flash 5/5 at every dose. Eight necessary reports: Lite 5/8, 5/8, 4/8, with a provider error included at the last dose. That last count is not four observed reasoning errors. One repetition; 8/32 preplanned identical-payload pairs elsewhere changed answers, all Lite. Sanitized assignment records . Follow-up and final expansion The initial follow-up and one final, outcome-independent expansion are both completed. The expansion used all four remaining worlds from the original screened seed prefix, with no model outcomes used in selection. Combined: 12 underlying worlds, six per stratum, 144 scored calls plus two initial probes . The expansion decision followed the initial result, so report phases separately and treat combined estimates as exploratory. At 0/100/1000 independent records: Initial four-report Lite: 7/8, 5/8, 7/8 ; extension: 3/4, 4/4, 3/4 ; combined: 10/12, 9/12, 10/12 . Initial eight-report Lite: 6/8, 3/8, 4/8 ; extension: 3/4, 2/4, 3/4 ; combined: 9/12, 5/12, 7/12 . Flash: every scored response correct in both phases and every dose; 12/12 per combined panel . This ceiling score is specific to these cases/settings. Each combined denominator twelve means two attempts on six worlds, not twelve independent worlds. The primary 1000-minus-zero Lite estimate remains 0 points : four worlds unchanged, one gains 0.5 and one loses 0.5. Descriptive 95% world bootstrap interval [-25, +25] points , exact sign-flip p=1.0. Equal observed accuracy does not establish equivalence or prove no effect. Necessary evidence, context length and composition do not isolate a general reasoning mechanism. The earlier aggregate improvement did not reproduce here. In the four-report stratum, mean estimated cost per scored call rose from less than $0.01 to $0.07 for Lite (about 56×), and less than $0.01 to $0.17 for Flash (about 77×), while zero- and 1000-record aggregate scores stayed unchanged. This is a useful bounded cost/robustness example, not a general law about reasoning. The combined receipt-based estimate is $6.96 , including $4.73 initially and $2.23 for the final expansion. The initial total includes $0.24 for the two probes. No unresolved holds; no transport or protocol failures. This is not a provider invoice. The total commitment preflight was $9.40 against the single $10.00 allowance; no further paid calls are planned. Replay from an installed wheel, without a repository, key or provider: clue-benchmark examples replay nuisance-followup --output runs/nuisance Add --figures with the figures extra. The output contains initial.json, extension.json, analysis.json and an accessible local HTML report with separate phase tables. The general examples replay measured-results gallery also includes these 144 saved assignments, preserving study/settings identities. Combined analysis and all sanitized assignments , and source/archive checksum index retain nulls, wrong answers and abstentions. Approvals, credentials, dispatch ledgers, provider prose and raw receipts are excluded. These are evaluator outcomes and must not be added to agent prompts. Initial study source archives remain immutable; the expansion and production code have distinct version/source identities. Certified burden Flash 30/30 in each 32-report path/tree arm; Lite 9/30 and 7/30. These are three attempts on ten worlds per arm. A simple heuristic solves some constructions. Necessary-report cost is not proof depth or model difficulty. High thinking differs from the motivating low-thinking pilot. Sanitized records . Hard cases and resources Fresh confirmation: 9/48 correct, 28 wrong, 11 abstentions, no provider/protocol errors, 48 independent worlds, 64 suspects, 455 interacting reports, 32768 output tokens including thinking. The 455 reports were not individually necessary. Estimated $7.23 belongs to a closed historical allowance. Fresh records . An earlier adaptive same-six-world comparison rose from 2/6 to 5/6 with more output allowance. Preserve adaptive status and resource differences. Adaptive records . Completion versus supported correctness Sampled Qwen: 67/72 valid final actions, 22 supported correct, 15 wrong with sufficient evidence, 11 appropriate abstentions, 19 unsupported answers including two lucky correct guesses, and five output-limit protocol failures. Three receipts were reused; 72 slots were not 72 fresh calls or independent worlds. On 29 matched returned slots completion rose 13/29 to 25/29 while supported correctness changed 13/29 to 12/29. More completed outputs did not imply better reasoning. Sanitized indexed outcomes permit count replay; full raw provider replay remains private/pending rights and sanitization review. Provenance and limits Source/checksum/sanitization index records original source paths and SHA-256 values plus hashes of the distribution copies. Only selected evaluator outcome fields are retained; no raw receipt, approval, checkpoint or model prose is shipped. These summaries are evaluator data and must not be placed in agent prompts. Hashes are integrity evidence, not ownership clearance. The original documents and frozen sources remain preserved. The owner authorized public visibility of the existing repository and its history; ignored operational archives remain local and are not uploaded. Licensing, outside reproduction and human template review remain pending. No inference occurs when reading or replaying these records.

docs.text: Open questions for the initial preview This is an early research preview of Clue Benchmark 0.5.0rc2. The measured results are preliminary; the software candidate, redistribution licenses and human reviews remain pending. The owner requested an initial public preview with those questions visible. This does not grant an open-source or dataset license or claim a PyPI release. Questions the experiments leave open Does irrelevant evidence ever help consistently? The original five-world Lite improvement did not repeat in the expanded follow-up. The primary endpoint change was zero, with a descriptive interval of [-25, +25] percentage points on six worlds. A larger, separately preregistered sample would be needed to distinguish a repeatable benefit from sampling and response variation. Why did individual worlds improve or worsen? Four primary worlds stayed unchanged, one improved and one worsened. These outcomes do not identify a reasoning mechanism. Content, order and context length need separate controls before attributing changes to distraction or useful extra computation. Is the harder-setting dip repeatable? Lite's 9/12 → 5/12 → 7/12 pattern at 0/100/1,000 irrelevant records is small and non-monotonic. Does it recur on fresh worlds, and how much is ordinary response variation? When does robustness become worth its cost? In the four-report setting, cost rose about 56× for Lite and 77× for Flash at 1,000 records without higher endpoint accuracy. Does that tradeoff change with useful redundancy, related distractors, other models or a different resource allowance? What makes a certified puzzle difficult for an agent? Minimum necessary evidence measures information burden, not proof depth or model difficulty. Which structural properties predict errors after controlling for simple construction heuristics, input length and output budget? How stable are results across resource settings and model versions? The adaptive six-world budget comparison and fresh 48-world hard confirmation answer different questions. Fresh matched comparisons are needed before generalizing across thinking/output allowances, formats or model revisions. Can agents learn to communicate the right evidence? Current star forwarding is programmed. It demonstrates delivery sufficiency, not learned collaboration or efficient communication policies. Do supported correctness and completion improve together? Qwen's matched returned slots showed more completed actions without higher supported correctness. Future work should retain lucky guesses, appropriate abstentions, wrong answers and protocol failures as separate outcomes. Do independent people interpret the rules as intended? Two independent template/rule reviews and an outside installation/replay run remain pending. Automated solver checks do not substitute for these reviews. These are proposed research questions, not registered experiments or authorized spending. The October 27 allowance is closed at an estimated $6.96 , with no holds and no further paid calls. Any future study requires a separate plan and budget. The documentation deployment excludes credentials, authorizations, ledgers and raw provider prose; ignored operational archives remain local and are not uploaded. Distribution: Which organization-owned PyPI and dataset accounts will host approved artifacts? Are protected environments, trusted publishing and final hosted dataset/Croissant checks configured? Final acceptance: Which exact source revision and artifact hashes will the owner approve for the complete release? Public preview availability does not clear these gates. What is available now? Generation prints a JSON summary with complete: true and validation prints status: verified . The preset requests one single-agent case with exactly four necessary reports.
